text: GRADUATION DAY In the year 1920, the student and the statesman saw many indications that the social, financial and industrial troubles that had vexed the United States of America for so long a time were about to culminate in civil war. \Vealth had grown so strong, that the few were about to strangle the many, and among the great masses of the people, there was sullen and rebellious discontent.
text_raw:
GRADUATION DAY
In the year 1920, the student and the statesman saw many indications that
the social, financial and industrial troubles that had vexed the United States of
America for so long a time were about to culminate in civil war.
\Vealth had grown so strong, that the few were about to strangle the many,
and among the great masses of the people, there was sullen and rebellious
discontent.

text: The laborer in the cities, the producer on the farm, the merchant, the professional man and all save organized capital and its satellites, saw a gloomy and hopeless future. \Vith these conditions prevailing, the graduation exercises of the class of 1920 of the National Military Academy at West Point, held for many a foreboding promise of momentous changes, but the 12th of June found the usual gay scene at the great institution overlooking the Hudson.
text_raw:
The laborer in the cities, the producer on the farm, the merchant, the
professional man and all save organized capital and its satellites, saw a gloomy
and hopeless future.
\Vith these conditions prevailing, the graduation exercises of the class of
1920 of the National Military Academy at West Point, held for many a
foreboding promise of momentous changes, but the 12th of June found the
usual gay scene at the great institution overlooking the Hudson.

text: The President of the Republic, his Secretary of War and many other distinguished guests were there to do honor to the occasion, together with friends, relatives and admirers of the young men who were being sent out to the ultimate leadership of the Nation's Army.
text_raw:
The President
of the Republic, his Secretary of War and many other distinguished guests were
there to do honor to the occasion, together with friends, relatives and admirers
of the young men who were being sent out to the ultimate leadership of the
Nation's Army.

text: The scene had all the usual charm of \Vest Point graduations, and the usual intoxicating atmosphere of military display.
text_raw:
The scene had all the usual charm of \Vest Point graduations,
and the usual intoxicating atmosphere of military display.

text: There was among the young graduating soldiers one who seemed depressed and out of touch with the triumphant blare of militarism, for he alone of his fellow classmen had there no kith nor kin to bid him God-speed in his new career.
text_raw:
There was among the young graduating soldiers one who seemed depressed
and out of touch with the triumphant blare of militarism, for he alone of his
fellow classmen had there no kith nor kin to bid him God-speed in his new
career.

text: Standing apart under the broad shadow of an oak, he looked out over long stretches of forest and river, but what he saw was his home in distant Kentucky-s-the old farmhouse that the sun and the rain and the lichens had softened into a mottled gray.
text_raw:
Standing apart under the broad shadow of an oak, he looked out over long
stretches of forest and river, but what he saw was his home in distant
Kentucky-s-the old farmhouse that the sun and the rain and the lichens had
softened into a mottled gray.

text: He saw the gleaming brook that wound its way through the tangle of orchard and garden, and parted the distant blue-grass meadow.
text_raw:
He saw the gleaming brook that wound its way
through the tangle of orchard and garden, and parted the distant blue-grass
meadow.

text: He saw his aged mother sitting under the honeysuckle trellis, book in hand, but thinking, he knew, of him.
text_raw:
He saw his aged mother sitting under the honeysuckle trellis, book in hand,
but thinking, he knew, of him.

text: And then there was the perfume of the flowers, the droning of the bees in the warm sweet air and the drowsy hound at his father's feet.
text_raw:
And then there was the perfume of the flowers,
the droning of the bees in the warm sweet air and the drowsy hound at his
father's feet.

text: But this was not all the young man saw, for Philip Dru, in spite of his military training, was a close student of the affairs of his country, and he saw that which raised grave doubts in his mind as to the outcome of his career.
text_raw:
But this was not all the young man saw, for Philip Dru, in spite of his
military training, was a close student of the affairs of his country, and he saw
that which raised grave doubts in his mind as to the outcome of his career.

text: He saw many of the civil institutions of his country debased by the power of wealth under the thin guise of the constitutional protection of property.

He
saw many of the civil institutions of his country debased by the power of wealth

text: He saw the Army which he had sworn to serve faithfully becoming prostituted by this same power, and used at times for purposes of intimidation and petty conquests where the interests of wealth were at stake.

text: The young man's eyes had become bright and hard, when his day-dream was interrupted, and he was looking into the gray-blue eyes of Gloria Strawn-the one whose lot he had been comparing to that of her sisters in the city, in the mills, the sweatshops, the big stores, and the streets.
text_raw:
The young man's eyes had become bright and hard, when his day-dream was
interrupted, and he was looking into the gray-blue eyes of Gloria Strawn-the
one whose lot he had been comparing to that of her sisters in the city, in the
mills, the sweatshops, the big stores, and the streets.

text: He had met her for the first time a few hours before, when his friend and classmate, Jack Strawn, had presented him to his sister.

He had met her for the first
time a few hours before, when his friend and classmate, Jack Strawn, had
presented him to his sister.

text: No comrade knew Dru better than Strawn, and no one admired him so much.
text_raw:
No comrade knew Dru better than Strawn, and no
one admired him so much.

text: Therefore, Gloria, ever seeking a closer contact with life, had come to \Vest Point eager to meet the lithe young Kentuckian, and to measure him by the other men of her acquaintance.
text_raw:
Therefore, Gloria, ever seeking a closer contact with
life, had come to \Vest Point eager to meet the lithe young Kentuckian, and to
measure him by the other men of her acquaintance.

text: She was disappointed in his appearance, for she had fancied him almost godÂ­ like in both size and beauty, and she saw a man of medium height, slender but toughly knit, and with a strong, but homely face. \Vhen he smiled and spoke she forgot her disappointment, and her interest revived, for her sharp city sense caught the trail of a new experience.
text_raw:
She was disappointed in his appearance, for she had fancied him almost godÂ­
like in both size and beauty, and she saw a man of medium height, slender but
toughly knit, and with a strong, but homely face. \Vhen he smiled and spoke she
forgot her disappointment, and her interest revived, for her sharp city sense
caught the trail of a new experience.

text: To Philip Dru, whose thought of and experience with women was almost nothing, so engrossed had he been in his studies, military and economic, Gloria seemed little more than a child.
text_raw:
To Philip Dru, whose thought of and experience with women was almost
nothing, so engrossed had he been in his studies, military and economic, Gloria
seemed little more than a child.

text: And yet her frank glance of appraisal when he had been introduced to her, and her easy though somewhat languid conversation on the affairs of the commencement, perplexed and slightly annoyed him.
text_raw:
And yet her frank glance of appraisal when he
had been introduced to her, and her easy though somewhat languid conversation

text_raw:
He
even felt some embarrassment in her presence.

text: Child though he knew her to be, he hesitated whether he should call her by her given name, and was taken aback when she smilingly thanked him for doing so, with the assurance that she was often bored with the eternal conventionality of people in her social circle.
text_raw:
Child though he knew her to be, he hesitated whether he should call her by
her given name, and was taken aback when she smilingly thanked him for doing
so, with the assurance that she was often bored with the eternal conventionality
of people in her social circle.

text: Suddenly turning from the commonplaces of the day, Gloria looked directly at Philip, and with easy self-possession turned the conversation to himself.
text_raw:
Suddenly turning from the commonplaces of the day, Gloria looked directly
at Philip, and with easy self-possession turned the conversation to himself.

text: "I am wondering, Mr. Dru, why you came to West Point and why it is you like the thought of being a soldier?" she asked.
text_raw:
"I am wondering, Mr. Dru, why you came to West Point and why it is you
like the thought of being a soldier?" she asked.

text: "An American soldier has to fight so seldom that I have heard that the insurance companies regard them as the best of risks, so what attraction, Mr. Dru, can a military career have for you?" Never before had Philip been asked such a question, and it surprised him that it should come from this slip of a girl, but he answered her in the serious strain of his thoughts.
text_raw:
"An American soldier has to
fight so seldom that I have heard that the insurance companies regard them as
the best of risks, so what attraction, Mr. Dru, can a military career have for
you?"
Never before had Philip been asked such a question, and it surprised him
that it should come from this slip of a girl, but he answered her in the serious
strain of his thoughts.

text: "-,\s far back as I can remember," he said, "I have wanted to be a soldier.
text_raw: "-,\s far back as I can remember," he said, "I have wanted to be a soldier.

text: It is the primitive man in me, I suppose, but sobered and enlightened by civilization.
text_raw:
It is the primitive man in me, I suppose, but sobered and enlightened

text: I would do everything in my power to avert war and the suffering it entails.
text_raw:

text: Fate, inclination, or what not has brought me here, and I hope my life may not be wasted, but that in God's own way, I may be a humble instrument for good.

text: "Nowhere in the world is wealth more defiant, and monopoly more insistent than in this mighty republic," he said, "and it is here that the next great battle for human emancipation will be fought and won.

THE VISION OF PHILIP DRU
Long before Philip had finished speaking, Gloria saw that he had forgotten
her presence. \Vith glistening eyes and face aflame he had talked on and on with
such compelling force that she beheld in him the prophet of a new day.

and at home have heard only the other side, while at school they mostly evade

received such an ovation that it stilled criticism, for it was plain that the new
order of things had to be accepted, and there was a thrill of fear among those
who would have liked to raise their voices in protest.

text: 79 CHAPTERXXX A NEW CODE OF LAWS Dru selected another board of five lawyers, and to them he gave the task of reforming legal procedure and of pruning down the existing laws, both State and National, cutting out the obsolete and useless ones and rewriting those recommended to be retained, in plain and direct language free from useless legal verbiage and understandable to the ordinary lay citizen.

79
CHAPTERXXX
A NEW CODE OF LAWS
Dru selected another board of five lawyers, and to them he gave the task of
reforming legal procedure and of pruning down the existing laws, both State and
National, cutting out the obsolete and useless ones and rewriting those
recommended to be retained, in plain and direct language free from useless legal
verbiage and understandable to the ordinary lay citizen.

text: He then created another board, of even greater ability, to read, digest and criticise the work of the other two boards and report their findings directly to him, giving a brief summary of their reasons and recommendations.

text: THE RAILROAD PROBLEM \Vhile the boards and commissions appointed by Administrator Dru were working out new tax, tariff and revenue laws, establishing the judiciary and legal machinery on a new basis and revising the general law, it was necessary that the financial system of the country also should be reformed.

financial system of the country also should be reformed.

text: Now in these cases I have quoted, and I could refer to many others, a unity of interest is established between labor and capital, with the result that there is a general atmosphere of peace and of mutual brotherhood and goodwill.

of interest is established between labor and capital, with the result that there is a

text: Capital receives the advantage of greater security.
text_raw: Capital receives the advantage of greater security.

text: WILLING AND UNWILLING SERVICE.

text: Now, what does the substitution of such conditions for the conditions generally prevailing to-day in England mean for our country? \V'ho shall estimate the difference between the value of willing and unwilling service?
text_raw:
Now, what does the substitution of such conditions for the conditions
generally prevailing to-day in England mean for our country? \V'ho shall estimate

text: The Board of Trade will tell you that a man paid by piecework is generally from 30 to 50 per cent. more effective than a man paid by time.
text_raw:
The Board of
Trade will tell you that a man paid by piecework is generally from 30 to 50 per
cent. more effective than a man paid by time.

text: If the co-partnership principle, which is better than piecework, because it tends to produce identity of interest between capital and labor were to increase the efficiency of time-paid workers from 30 to 50 per cent., just think of the result; and yet the fact that co-partnership might add from 30 to 50 per cent. to the efficiency of the worker is urged by many trade unionists as a reason against co-partnership.
text_raw:
If the co-partnership principle, which is better than piecework, because it
tends to produce identity of interest between capital and labor were to increase

text: They seem to fear that the result of making men co-partners will be to cause them to give 25 per cent. better labor and to receive only 50 per cent. more wage.
text_raw:
They seem to fear that the result of making men co-partners will
be to cause them to give 25 per cent. better labor and to receive only 50 per
cent. more wage.

text: No system can be right which is based on the assumption that self-interest calls for a man to give his worst instead of his best.
text_raw:
No system can be right which is based on the assumption that
self-interest calls for a man to give his worst instead of his best.

text: When I compare Canada with England I am struck by the fact, that, whereas Canada's greatest undeveloped asset is her natural resources, England's greatest undeveloped asset is man himself.
text_raw:
When I compare
Canada with England I am struck by the fact, that, whereas Canada's greatest
undeveloped asset is her natural resources, England's greatest undeveloped asset
is man himself.

text: How to get each man to do his best is the problem before England to-day.
text_raw:
How to get each man to do his best is the problem before
England to-day.

text: It is because co-partnership harnesses to industry not only the muscle but the heart and the intelligence of the worker that we are justified in regarding it with reverence and enthusiasm as the principle of the future.

muscle but the heart and the intelligence of the worker that we are justified in
